_doc: The applicability vocabulary. Every tag a chapter or item may name in 'Applies when' / 'Requires'. kind: asset = a fact about one deployment, settled per asset; capability = something the operator or lab provides, settled per engagement (false => 'blocked', not 'n/a'); programme = a rule of the bounty programme, settled per engagement. auto: the fingerprinter (scripts/sane fp) can set it true on evidence; auto_false: the fingerprinter may also set it false. needs: when this expression is false the fact is false without a probe. probe: the cheapest observation that settles it.

http.desc: Answers HTTP or HTTPS on some port
http.probe: sane fp <host> (GET / on 80 and 443, plus any web port from the port scan)

app.desc: A dynamic application: server-side state, sessions, forms, user input reaches a backend
app.probe: sane fp <host>; confirm by browsing: does any request change server state or return per-user data?

api.desc: Serves a machine API (JSON, XML, gRPC-web) that takes parameters
api.probe: content-type of XHR/fetch responses in the proxy history; sane fp reports JSON roots and API path patterns found in JS

static.desc: Only static content: marketing pages, docs, a bucket or CDN origin with no backend logic
static.probe: sane fp <host>: no cookies set, no forms posting to the host, no XHR to same-site API

spa.desc: JavaScript-heavy front end (React, Vue, Angular, Next) whose bundles hold the route and API map
spa.probe: sane fp <host>: script bundle count and size, framework markers

default-page.desc: Only a web-server default page, a bare 403/404, or a parked page at every path tried
default-page.probe: sane fp <host>: body hash of / equals body hash of a random path, or matches a default-page signature

redirect-only.desc: Every path redirects to another host
redirect-only.probe: sane fp <host>: / and a random path both 30x to a different host

ip.desc: The asset is a bare IP address or came from a CIDR range, with no host name of its own
ip.probe: set by sane asset add / sane recon

nonweb-ports.desc: At least one non-HTTP service is reachable (SSH, FTP, SMTP, a database, Redis, RDP, ...)
nonweb-ports.probe: sane ports <host> (naabu or nmap top ports at the engagement rate limit)

cdn.desc: Fronted by a CDN (Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly, CloudFront, ...)
cdn.probe: sane fp <host>: response headers and CNAME

cache.desc: A shared cache stores responses: Age, X-Cache, CF-Cache-Status: HIT, or a repeat request served faster with identical Date
cache.probe: request a static path twice with a cache buster and compare Age / X-Cache / CF-Cache-Status

waf.desc: A WAF blocks or challenges obvious payloads
waf.probe: sane fp <host> sends one benign canary (?x=<script>alert(1)</script>) and compares status and body with the baseline

reverse-proxy.desc: Requests pass through a front end (load balancer, CDN, nginx, HAProxy) before the application server
reverse-proxy.probe: Via / X-Forwarded-* echoes, Server header that differs between error classes, a CDN in front

cname-3p.desc: DNS points at a third-party service the organisation must claim (GitHub Pages, Heroku, S3, Azure, Fastly, Zendesk, ...)
cname-3p.probe: dig +short CNAME <host>; compare with the takeover service list

dangling.desc: The DNS target does not resolve, or the third-party service answers with its 'unclaimed' page
dangling.probe: dig the CNAME target; fetch the host and match the service's unclaimed fingerprint

cloud-storage.desc: Bucket or blob URLs (S3, GCS, Azure Blob, DigitalOcean Spaces, Firebase) appear in responses, JS or DNS
cloud-storage.probe: sane fp <host> greps responses and bundles for storage host names

java.probe: JSESSIONID, Whitelabel error page, .do/.action/.jsp, stack traces

node.probe: X-Powered-By: Express, connect.sid, Next.js server, error format

python.probe: csrftoken/sessionid cookies, Werkzeug/gunicorn/uvicorn Server header, error pages

cms.desc: An off-the-shelf CMS or e-commerce platform (WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, Magento, AEM, Sitecore, ...)

known-product.desc: An identifiable third-party product or framework with a version (Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, GitLab, Grafana, Spring Boot, Tomcat, ...)
known-product.probe: sane fp <host>: title, favicon hash, headers, well-known paths

graphql.probe: POST {"query":"{__typename}"} to /graphql, /api/graphql, /v1/graphql, /query, /gql and any path named in JS bundles

websocket.probe: grep bundles for wss:// and new WebSocket(; look for 101 responses in the proxy history

api-docs.probe: sane fp <host> tries the usual documentation paths

source-maps.probe: sourceMappingURL comment in a bundle, or <bundle>.map answers 200

jwt.desc: JWTs carry identity or authorisation (cookie, Authorization header, URL, local storage)
jwt.probe: grep cookies, headers and bundles for eyJ...; decode the header

serialized.desc: Serialized objects cross the trust boundary: Java (rO0AB / ac ed), .NET ViewState or BinaryFormatter, PHP (O:8:), Python pickle, Ruby Marshal, YAML
serialized.probe: grep cookies, hidden fields and parameters for the magic prefixes

xml-input.desc: Some endpoint parses XML the client supplies: SOAP, SAML, RSS/sitemap import, SVG/DOCX/XLSX upload, or JSON endpoints that also accept application/xml
xml-input.probe: content types in the proxy history; resend one JSON request as XML and read the error

login.desc: The asset authenticates users (its own login, or an SSO hand-off)
login.probe: a password field, a /login or /signin route, a 401 with WWW-Authenticate, or an auth API in the bundles

signup.desc: Anyone can register an account (self-service or free trial)
signup.probe: look for a register / sign-up / start-trial route and complete it with a programme-approved email alias

password-reset.desc: A forgot-password or account-recovery flow exists
password-reset.probe: the login page links to it

mfa.desc: 2FA / MFA / OTP can be enabled or is enforced
mfa.probe: account security settings; login asks for a code

oauth-login.desc: The app logs users in through a third party or its own IdP with OAuth/OIDC ('Sign in with ...'), i.e. it is an OAuth client
oauth-login.probe: login buttons; requests carrying client_id, redirect_uri, response_type, state

oauth-provider.desc: The asset is an authorisation server: third-party apps obtain tokens from it (/oauth/authorize, /.well-known/openid-configuration, app registration)
oauth-provider.probe: GET /.well-known/openid-configuration and /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; a developer or 'connected apps' section

saml.probe: SAMLRequest / SAMLResponse parameters, /saml/ or /sso/ routes, enterprise SSO settings

cookie-auth.desc: The session rides in a cookie the browser attaches automatically
cookie-auth.probe: replay an authenticated request with only the cookies, then with only the Authorization header

api-keys.desc: Users can create API keys, personal access tokens or app passwords

roles.desc: More than one privilege level exists (admin, member, viewer, support, ...)
roles.probe: team or user-management settings; role fields in the profile API response

multi-tenant.desc: Data is partitioned by organisation, workspace, team, shop or project
multi-tenant.probe: an org or workspace id in paths, hosts or bodies; an 'invite teammate' feature

object-ids.desc: Requests name objects by an identifier the client supplies (numeric id, UUID, slug, file name, email)
object-ids.probe: any authenticated request in the proxy history with an id in the path, query or body

invite.desc: Invitations, share links or access tokens grant other people access to a resource
invite.probe: invite or share buttons; tokenised URLs

params.desc: Server-side endpoints take parameters (query, body, path, header) that influence the response
params.probe: any non-static request in the proxy history or crawl

reflect.desc: Some request input is written back into an HTML or JavaScript response
reflect.probe: sane fp sends a unique marker in common parameters; grep responses for it

user-content.desc: Content one user stores is rendered to another user or to staff (profiles, comments, tickets, file names, messages)
user-content.probe: any field you fill in that a second account or an admin can see

rich-text.desc: A field accepts markup: HTML, Markdown, BBCode, SVG, MathML, a WYSIWYG editor
rich-text.probe: an editor toolbar, or markup that survives a save

upload.probe: file inputs, multipart requests, pre-signed upload URLs

file-param.desc: A parameter names a file, path, template, language or include (file=, path=, template=, lang=, page=, doc=)
file-param.probe: grep the crawl and proxy history for such parameter names and for values that look like paths

file-processing.desc: The server transforms supplied files: image resize, video transcode, archive extraction, document conversion or parsing, repository import
file-processing.probe: upload an image and compare the stored bytes; look for thumbnails, previews, 'import from zip'

url-fetch.desc: The server requests a URL the user supplies: webhooks, import by URL, link previews, avatar from URL, PDF or screenshot rendering, feed readers, integrations
url-fetch.probe: grep the proxy history for parameters whose value is a URL; walk settings for webhooks, integrations and import features

render.desc: User-controlled content is rendered server-side into a PDF, image, e-mail or document (headless browser, wkhtmltopdf, LaTeX)
render.probe: export, invoice, report or 'download as PDF' features; PDF producer metadata

template-input.desc: Users can edit templates or formats the server later evaluates: e-mail templates, notification text with variables, themes, report layouts
template-input.probe: settings pages that show {{variable}} style placeholders

redirect-param.desc: A parameter controls where the user is sent next (next=, url=, return=, redirect_uri=, continue=, dest=)
redirect-param.probe: grep the crawl for such names; watch the login and logout flows

state-change.desc: Authenticated requests change state (the normal case for any app with accounts)
state-change.probe: any POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE in an authenticated session

cors-headers.probe: sane fp sends Origin: https://sane-probe.example on / and discovered API paths

postmessage.desc: Front-end code registers a message event listener or calls postMessage

email-out.desc: The app e-mails links or content built from the request (reset, invite, verification, notifications)
email-out.probe: trigger a reset or invite to an inbox you control and read the raw message

payments.desc: Money or value moves: checkout, pricing plans, credits, coupons, gift cards, refunds, payouts
payments.probe: a pricing page, a cart, billing settings

limited-action.desc: Some action is meant to succeed a limited number of times: redeem a code, claim a bonus, vote, withdraw, use an invite, start a trial
limited-action.probe: any feature whose rules say 'once', 'per user' or 'while balance lasts'

plans.desc: Tiered subscription plans gate features (free, pro, enterprise; trials; add-ons)
plans.probe: a pricing or upgrade page; plan or tier fields in the account API; 'upgrade to unlock' prompts

quota.desc: Counted limits are enforced per account or plan: seats, projects, storage, API calls, messages
quota.probe: usage meters in settings; 'limit reached' responses; counters in the account API

refunds.desc: Users can obtain money or credit back themselves: refund, cancellation with refund, downgrade credit, withdrawal
refunds.probe: order or billing pages with refund, cancel or withdraw actions

multi-currency.desc: More than one currency or regional price list is offered
multi-currency.probe: a currency or country selector; a currency field in cart or checkout requests

approval-flow.desc: Some action needs a second person's approval before it takes effect (maker-checker, review, moderation)
approval-flow.probe: 'pending approval' states; approve and reject actions in the UI or API

verification.desc: Features are gated on a verified e-mail address, phone number or identity
verification.probe: 'verify your e-mail to continue' prompts; a verified flag in the profile API

export.desc: The application produces per-user downloadable files: data exports, reports, invoices, receipts, backups
export.probe: export, download or 'email me my data' features; links to generated files in responses or e-mails

ai-feature.desc: An LLM-backed feature takes user or third-party content: chatbot, assistant, summariser, agent with tools
ai-feature.probe: chat widgets, 'AI' labelled features, streaming completion endpoints

admin-panel.desc: An administrative or internal-tool interface is reachable
admin-panel.probe: content discovery; titles such as admin, dashboard, console, internal

account.desc: We hold at least one working test account on this asset
account.probe: engagement.json accounts[]; register one with the programme's e-mail alias rule if sign-up is open

two-accounts.desc: We hold two independent accounts (attacker A and victim B), in different tenants where tenants exist

priv-accounts.desc: We hold accounts at two different privilege levels in the same tenant (for example admin and member)

oob.desc: An out-of-band interaction server is available (interactsh-client or a host we control) for blind SSRF, XXE, RCE and XSS callbacks

browser.desc: A scriptable browser is available (Playwright, Chrome DevTools MCP) to prove client-side findings and capture screenshots

purchase.desc: We can complete a payment on this asset: sandbox or test card numbers the programme provides, or a real purchase the operator has approved
purchase.probe: the policy's testing notes; ask the operator; record in engagement.json

code-host-token.desc: A GitHub or GitLab API token is available for authenticated code search across public repositories
code-host-token.probe: GH_TOKEN or GITLAB_TOKEN in the environment

takeover-ok.desc: The programme accepts subdomain takeover reports

bruteforce-ok.desc: The programme allows credential brute forcing or large-volume rate-limit proofs

exclusions._doc: Programme exclusion tags. engagement.json exclusions[] lists the ones the policy names; an item whose 'Excluded by' row names one of them is closed as 'excluded' without a test.
exclusions.clickjacking: Clickjacking / UI redressing on pages without sensitive actions (or the whole class)
exclusions.self-xss: Self-XSS and XSS that needs unlikely user interaction
exclusions.csrf-low: Login/logout CSRF and CSRF on non-sensitive actions
exclusions.rate-limit: Missing rate limiting / brute force findings
exclusions.missing-headers: Missing security headers, cookie flags, CSP weaknesses without an exploit
exclusions.host-header: Host header injection without demonstrated impact
exclusions.cors: CORS findings without demonstrated data theft
exclusions.ssl-tls: TLS configuration, weak ciphers, certificate issues
exclusions.version-disclosure: Banner, version or stack-trace disclosure without impact
exclusions.takeover: Subdomain takeover (or takeover without a working claim)
exclusions.third-party: Bugs in third-party services or assets the organisation does not control
exclusions.known-cve: Known CVEs within the programme's patch window, or without a working exploit
exclusions.social-engineering: Anything requiring social engineering or phishing of staff or users
exclusions.leaked-credentials: Credentials found in third-party breaches or public dumps
exclusions.automated: Reports from automated scanners without a manual proof
exclusions.session-expiry: Session timeout and logout-related session handling
exclusions.prompt-injection: LLM prompt injection without a security impact beyond the attacker's own session
exclusions.promo-abuse: Abuse of trials, coupons, referral bonuses or promotions, including through multiple accounts
exclusions.internal-info: Disclosure of internal host names, private IP addresses, software paths or file metadata (EXIF) without further impact
